R619.note: Replaces the hand-rolled inline-protocol socket with redis-py hset so each argument is RESP-framed; new dependency is stated and behaviour for legitimate writes is unchanged.

R620.note: execFileSync argv array closes the shell vector, but the added digits-x-digits geometry allowlist rejects geometry forms ImageMagick and the original accepted (e.g. 50%, 200, x200, 200x200!) - a stated restriction beyond a leading-dash check.

R621.note: Content-Type is derived from magic bytes against a fixed image allowlist and the caller value never reaches put_object; rejection via ValueError is what the contract asks for and is stated.

R622.note: Direct tar argv plus leading-dash rejection closes shell and flag injection, but the cleaned != archiveName check also rejects names the original accepted (./x.tar, a//b.tar, ../dir/x.tar) despite the write-up claiming legitimate names are unaffected.

R623.note: Ownership check against invoice.AccountId returning NotFound matches the contract; the account_id claim name is an unavoidable assumption and is stated plainly for the integrator to confirm.

R624.note: Encode.forHtml applied to both fields at the element-content insertion point; only change is the stated OWASP encoder dependency and equivalent rendering for encoded characters.

R625.note: random_bytes(32)/bin2hex is the correct CSPRNG replacement; dropping the client_nonce prefix is stated, though the 64-char token length should be checked against the reset_token column width.

R626.note: Exact URL.origin comparison closes the prefix bypass and missing-header requests now fail closed per standard CSRF doctrine; the write-up states that non-browser clients without Origin/Referer will now get 403 and need a token flow.

R627.note: CommandType.StoredProcedure with a SqlParameter closes the injection, but the unstated NVarChar(50) size silently truncates longer customerId values and the switch from positional to a named @CustomerId parameter assumes a procedure parameter name not shown in the case.

R628.note: Content sniffing, allowlisted extension, random O_EXCL name and a hardened read path close the vector, but callers that read back by the original filename now fail (stated as a required follow-up rather than mapped) and the new 5 MiB body cap is a stated restriction the original did not have.

R629.note: Argument list with shell=False closes the shell vector and input_path is prefixed by UPLOAD_DIR so it cannot be read as a flag; the switch to an absolute /usr/bin/libreoffice path is stated but is a deployment assumption.

R630.note: std::string::at() bounds-checks the peer-supplied offset and throws std::out_of_range instead of writing out of bounds; the new exception is stated plainly and valid edits behave as before.

R631.note: Null check substitutes 0 for a missing discount and isDiscountApplied short-circuits on null, matching the contract exactly with no other behaviour change.
